Building setting out (also called staking out or construction layout) is the process of transferring the exact positions and dimensions from architectural drawings to the actual site. This involves marking building corners, column grid lines, floor levels, setback distances, and other critical construction reference points using Total Station and levelling instruments.

Without accurate setting out, a building could be constructed in the wrong location, at wrong orientations, or violating setback regulations. Setting out errors can result in expensive demolition, structural compromise, or legal non-compliance with building permits. It is the critical first step that ensures every subsequent construction activity is correctly positioned.

Differential GPS surveying delivering centimetre-level positional accuracy for large-scale infrastructure, government, and industrial projects across Tamil Nadu.

Differential GPS (DGPS) is an enhancement to standard GPS that uses a network of fixed ground-based reference stations to broadcast the difference between GPS satellite positions and known fixed positions. This correction data, applied in real-time or post-processing, delivers centimetre-level horizontal and vertical accuracy far beyond standard GPS.

Standard GPS provides accuracy of only 5-10 metres, which is insufficient for engineering and land survey applications. DGPS corrects satellite errors, atmospheric delays, and clock variations to achieve 1-5 cm accuracy — essential for large-scale topographic mapping, control surveys, GIS data collection, and infrastructure alignment work.

Government survey departments, highway engineers, railway authorities, pipeline companies, large real estate developers, solar park developers, environmental agencies, and any organization requiring sub-decimetre accuracy over large areas.
Accurate Measurements — 1-5 cm positional accuracy in both horizontal and vertical planes
Legal Compliance — Control points established per SOI and revenue department norms
Faster Project Execution — Large areas surveyed rapidly compared to traditional methods
Reduced Construction Errors — Accurate control network prevents cumulative survey errors
Government Approval Support — Coordinates in WGS84/UTM as required by survey authorities

What is the difference between GPS and DGPS?
Standard GPS gives 5-10m accuracy. DGPS uses correction signals from reference stations to achieve 1-5 cm accuracy, making it suitable for engineering and survey applications.

Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) GPS is a DGPS variant that delivers centimetre accuracy in real-time, eliminating the need for post-processing. We use both RTK and static DGPS depending on project requirements.
Can DGPS work in forested or urban areas?
DGPS requires a clear sky view for best accuracy. In areas with obstructions, we supplement with Total Station measurements to ensure complete coverage.
What coordinate system do you use?
We deliver coordinates in WGS84, UTM (Universal Transverse Mercator), or local state plane systems as per project requirements and survey authority specifications.
How many control points can you establish per day?
Using RTK methods, we can establish 200-500 control points per day depending on terrain and point density requirements.

Electronic distance measurement and precise angle calculations using high-tech Total Station instruments for construction, engineering and cadastral surveys.
What is a Total Station Survey?

A Total Station is an electronic/optical instrument that combines an electronic theodolite (for measuring angles) with an electronic distance measurement (EDM) device. It can simultaneously measure horizontal and vertical angles and slope distances, computing horizontal distances and elevations. Total Stations are the workhorse instrument of modern field surveying.

Total Station surveys offer unmatched precision for all construction setting-out, traversing, topographic detail surveys, and boundary measurements in areas where GPS signals are unavailable or obstructed. They are especially critical for urban construction, underground surveys, and any project requiring millimetre-level accuracy.

Civil engineers, construction companies, infrastructure developers, architects, tunnel and underground works contractors, urban building project managers, and any organization requiring extremely precise on-site measurement.

What is a Total Station instrument?
A Total Station is an electronic survey instrument that simultaneously measures angles and distances to compute coordinates of survey points without manual chaining.
When is a Total Station preferred over GPS?
In urban areas, indoors, under dense canopy cover, or when millimetre accuracy is needed, Total Station is preferred as GPS signals may be blocked or inaccurate.
Can Total Station be used for setting out buildings?
Yes. Total Stations are the primary tool for building setting-out — precisely marking column positions, building corners, and structural reference points on-site.
How accurate is a Total Station?
Professional Total Stations achieve 1-5 mm distance accuracy and 1-5 arc-second angular accuracy, suitable for precision construction and engineering applications.
Can it be used at night?
Yes. Modern robotic Total Stations with laser distance measurement can operate in low light or complete darkness using reflectors and automated target tracking.
